meta.methodology: Read framework.md, the analyze-torah command, and the full source text torah_274.txt. Searched torahData.js for all edges where reference===274 AND type==='bechina' — result: zero edges. Read the source text for every concept the Rebbe explicitly equates using bechina language or structural equivalence. The teaching does not use the word 'בְּחִינַת' anywhere, but it does structurally equate two terms for the same inextinguishable Jewish spark (see below). All other relationships in this Torah are eitza (causal) in nature and are not counted as bechina nodes.

additions.reason: This is the central concept of the entire Torah and one of two poles of its core bechina equivalence. The Rebbe identifies this as the holy point of Jewish holiness that resides within every Jew — even a complete sinner (רָשָׁע גָּמוּר). It is called a 'נְקֻדָּה' (a point/spark) to indicate that it cannot be extinguished or uprooted. The Rebbe then re-names this exact same concept later in the same sentence as 'הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם' — the Judaism within them. This cross-naming is a structural bechina equivalence: the 'holy point of Jewish holiness' and 'the Judaism within them' are the same underlying reality, described from two different angles (one ontological, one experiential). This node is the dominant concept of this Torah's only cluster. It belongs in the proposed good package of the inextinguishable Jewish spark.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֲדַיִן בְּתוֹכָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִים

additions.reason: This is the second pole of the Torah's core bechina equivalence. The Rebbe re-states the very same concept introduced as 'הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה' at the opening of the sentence and now names it 'הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם' (the Judaism within them) at the close of the same paragraph. Both expressions describe the same reality: the irreducible, ineradicable Jewish essence that cannot be silenced even in the most complete sinner. The two names are two faces of the same thing — the ontological (holy point) and the experiential/ethnic (the Judaism) — making this a bechina pair. This node is the second member of the proposed package.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם אֵינָהּ מַנַּחַת אוֹתָם, וּמְבַלְבֶּלֶת אוֹתָם תָּמִיד

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states that the holy point 'brings them thoughts of repentance' (מְבִיאָה בָּהֶם הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה). This is an eitza statement (the holy point PRODUCES repentance-thoughts), not a bechina. However, as a concept named as the direct product of the holy point, it is the closest neighbor node in the Torah's conceptual landscape. It belongs in the good domain as an effect generated by the holy spark. It is listed here as a gap-concept the dataset should contain for completeness, though its relationship to the holy point is eitza, not bechina, and it would therefore constitute a separate node linked to the package by an eitza edge rather than a bechina edge.
additions.source_quote: מְבִיאָה בָּהֶם הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וְיִרְאָה מֵאֵימַת הַדִּין הַגָּדוֹל

additions.reason: Complete heresy (כְּפִירָה גְּמוּרָה) is the goal the wicked laboriously strive to reach — the state of having no remaining doubt toward the Truth (בְּלִי שׁוּם סָפֵק אֶל הָאֱמֶת). The Rebbe presents it as the evil mirror-destination of the teaching: what the sinner desires is the polar opposite of the נְקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה. In the Torah's structure, כְּפִירָה גְּמוּרָה is the destination of the evil effort — to silence the holy point entirely. It is an evil-domain concept and the natural counterpart to the good package. Its relationship to the holy point is eitza in reverse: the sinners labor to destroy the effect of the נְקֻדָּה by achieving כְּפִירָה. It would require its own evil-polarity package or edge in the dataset.
additions.source_quote: כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּגִּיעוּ לִכְפִירָה גְּמוּרָה בְּדַעְתָּם, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בְּאֹפֶן שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם עוֹד צַד סָפֵק לִנְטוֹת אֶל הָאֱמֶת

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל — the holy point of Jewish holiness present within every Jew; one of the two poles of the Torah's structural bechina equivalence. The dominant concept of this Torah. Not in the dataset.

הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם — 'the Judaism within them'; the second name for the same inextinguishable Jewish spark. The Rebbe uses this term to close the same paragraph in which he opened with 'נְקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה', making the two names structural bechina equivalents. Not in the dataset.
הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה — thoughts/stirrings of repentance; the eitza-product of the holy point that disturbs the sinners. Relationship to the holy point is eitza, not bechina. Not in the dataset.
יִרְאָה מֵאֵימַת הַדִּין הַגָּדוֹל — fear from the great Judgment; listed together with repentance-thoughts as what the holy point brings to the sinners. Eitza-product. Not in the dataset.
כְּפִירָה גְּמוּרָה — complete heresy; the evil goal the wicked labor to reach — full disconnection from Truth. The evil-domain mirror of the holy point. Not in the dataset.
רְשָׁעִים — the wicked; the subject of the teaching. Not itself a bechina node but the narrative subject.
analysis_notes.zero_edges_note: The dataset contains NO bechina edges for Torah #274. The entire teaching is unrepresented. The Torah's core structural bechina equation — הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה = הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם — is the minimum that needs to be captured as a bechina edge in torahData.js. The two nodes listed first in 'additions' above are the primary candidates for a meaningful bechina representation of this Torah in the map.
analysis_notes.bechina_identification_note: Torah #274 does not use the explicit word 'בְּחִינַת' anywhere in the text. The bechina equivalence between 'הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה' and 'הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם' is structural: the Rebbe opens one sentence by naming the concept as 'the holy point of Jewish holiness' and closes that same sentence by naming it 'the Judaism within them,' with both descriptions doing identical work in the argument — both cause the same disturbance (מְבַלְבֶּלֶת), both prevent the sinners from resting. This cross-naming of the same reality with two labels is the Rebbe's bechina technique even without the explicit word.
analysis_notes.teaching_summary: Torah #274 is a compact and psychologically acute teaching about the ineradicability of the Jewish soul. The Rebbe observes that even confirmed sinners who actively try to achieve complete heresy cannot succeed quickly, because the holy point / Judaism within them constantly disturbs them with thoughts of repentance and fear of judgment. Some of those who finally achieve complete heresy immediately die, and then see the Truth. The teaching's structure is almost entirely eitza (causal narrative), with a single structural bechina equivalence at its center: the holy point = the Judaism within. There is a good/evil polarity implied — the holy spark (good) versus complete heresy (evil) — but neither the good nor evil pole is developed into a full multi-node bechina cluster in the source text.
